hints: Focus on what type of alcohol can form a ketone on oxidation with acidified dichromate(VI).
Remember primary gives aldehyde then acid, secondary gives ketone, and tertiary shows no reaction, so check the position of the -OH in each name.
Now count the total carbons including branches, you need a secondary alcohol whose skeleton adds up to exactly six carbons.
walkthrough:
**Recall the oxidation rule**

Think of oxidation as removing hydrogens from the carbon with the -OH group. A secondary alcohol has the pattern $\text{R}_2\text{CHOH}$ and oxidises to a ketone $\text{R}_2\text{C=O}$.

Rule:
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O], \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 / \text{H}^+} \text{ketone}$$

**Classify each alcohol**

Look at the number in the name, it tells you where the -OH is. A 1-ol is primary, a 2-ol or 3-ol can be secondary or tertiary depending on branching.

$$\text{A: 1-ol = primary, B: 3-ol = secondary, C: 2-ol = secondary, D: 3-ol on fully branched C = tertiary}$$

**Count total carbons and conclude**

Add the parent chain plus all methyl branches. You need 6 carbons total for a 6-carbon ketone.

$$\text{A: 4 + 2 = 6C but primary, B: 5 + 1 = 6C and secondary, C: 5 + 2 = 7C, D: 5 + 1 = 6C but tertiary}$$
Only the 6-carbon secondary alcohol fits both conditions, so it gives a 6-carbon ketone.

options.A: 2,2-dimethylbutan-1-ol has 6 carbons in total (4 + 2) but the -OH is on C1, so it is a primary alcohol. It oxidises to an aldehyde then a carboxylic acid, not a ketone.
options.B: 2-methylpentan-3-ol has 6 carbons in total (5 + 1) and the -OH is on C3 attached to two other carbons, so it is secondary. Oxidation with acidified dichromate(VI) removes the H from C3 to give 2-methylpentan-3-one, a ketone with six carbons.
options.C: 3,3-dimethylpentan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol so it does give a ketone, but it has 7 carbons in total (5 + 2). The product is a 7-carbon ketone, not a 6-carbon ketone.
options.D: 3-methylpentan-3-ol has 6 carbons but C3 is attached to three other carbons (two from the chain plus the methyl), so it is a tertiary alcohol. It has no H on the C-OH to remove and is not oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI).
